Currently making the rounds in the Conservative quarter of my social media circles is an article at The Tee titled Not So Fast, Trudeau: We Need a Referendum on Electoral Reform: No matter which system Liberals choose, Canadians should have the final say..

Personally I thnk the idea of a national referendum on this matter, and a great many other matters, is a great idea - the best democracy is direct democracy. But to call the idea of the Government of the Day changing the electoral system "undemocratic" is more than just a bt of a stretch.

Lets look at how people voted.

  1. Liberal Party of Canada campaigned on electoral reform, it was a major plank in their platform and they took 39.5% of the popular vote.

  2. The NDP campaigned on electoral reform, it was a signifiant plank in their campaign and they took 19.7% of the popular vote.

  3. The Green Party campaigned on electoral reform, and they took 3.4% of the popular vote.

A little basic math tells us that among Canadians who voted almost 63% voted for a party campaigning on electoral reform, so how is mounting a national consultative process to determine which form of proportional representation Canadians would like to see with an eye to implementing that reform undemocratic?

Answer: It's not.

One could, I suppose, say quite reasonably that we just had a national referendum - on a number of issues - and now the losing side is disputing the results. Where I come from we call that sour grapes.
We don't need a national referendum on a new electoral system, I believe we should have one, but we don't need it.

I saw OP's complaint that /v/askvoat was a circlejerk. So I'm going to play the devil's advocate for y'all.

Although it may be true that less than 3% of gun violence is done by legally-obtained firearms, it is completely irrelevant to the discussion of imposing gun control; no sane liberal ever argues that gun violence is directly caused by responsible gun owners.

Instead, what most reasonable liberals believe, is that the reason the USA has so many illegal firearms is due to an abundance of poorly-regulated legal firearms sales. In other words, people who are quite obviously not the average, responsible gun owner can easily find ways to get a gun.

Their proposed solution, therefore, is simple ~ if there were more limits on the liquidity of guns, making it less easy for guns to change hands without the government noting things down, less legal guns would be able to fly under the radar and enter the wrong (illegal) hands.

In other words: Gun Control's final aims would not be to tackle the 3% of legal guns, but to tackle the ways in which legal guns become illegal guns, thereby causing 97% of gun crimes.

No one ever accused responsible gun owners of being directly responsible for mass shootings and whatnot. Nor is gun control designed specifically to take away gun owner's rights; that is merely an unfortunate side-effect of the bureaucracy involved in limiting gun sales.
